acceptanceCriteria: Decide and document in docs/DOGFOOD.md which BASE a merged-forward lane binds against (the last merged origin/main commit, or the merge-base of HEAD and origin/main) and what the CEM then attests
ocm-prepare names the bound that fired (git-operation budget vs output bound) and the measured size, so the fix: line can say what to do
Either make dogfood-change compute that BASE automatically when BASE..HEAD contains merge commits from main, or refuse early with the recommended BASE before running the expensive passes
body: Observed 2026-10-12 on the V1-1278 S1 lane (branch claude/v1-1278-s1-core, PR beamfall/corvint#850). The lane's dispatch BASE was d67ee35d4b126fe9432604a70b00c3e1efd2dba7. After two plain merges of origin/main (351c1396, 8a1b5361) the range d67ee35d..HEAD covered 130 files, 228 hunks and a 1.33 MB patch, all but 37 files merged from main. make dogfood-change BASE=d67ee35d then stopped at ocm-prepare-001 and ocm-prepare-002 with unsupported-resource-limit; cem-cite itself passed with a full 228-hunk plan. Which bound fired (the stable verifier git operation budget, default 1024, or an output bound) was not identified. Recovery used: bind against 4e609405e9eb362c3affac556a77800f9a3e9018, the origin/main commit merged last, whose diff is exactly the lane's change (37 files, 88 hunks); dogfood-change rc 0, dogfood-check PASS 88/88 supported, dogfood-seal PASS. docs/DOGFOOD.md tells a lane to bind against its unmoved BASE, which does not hold once a lane outlives a few merges on a busy main. Friction, not a defect in the bound itself: the bound is doing its job on the merged-in diff. Evidence: scratchpad agent-1278/dogfood/m-pass*.log on the orchestrating host; build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-12-v1-1278-s1-remove-0x-core.md.
title: Long-lived lane that merges origin/main cannot bind against its unmoved BASE: ocm-prepare stops with unsupported-resource-limit on a 228-hunk BASE..HEAD
